card.architecture: Qwen-Image 20B MMDiT edit model (Qwen2.5-VL encoder), masked to a painted region via InpaintModelConditioning — full instruction editing + reference images inside the mask only
card.summary: Paint a region, give an instruction, and optionally attach reference images — the Qwen edit runs only inside the mask and everything outside is composited back untouched. Unlike the base Qwen-Image inpaint (ControlNet, no references), this rides the Edit fine-tune, so you can say 'put the chair from image 2 here' and it edits the masked area with full reference/instruction understanding.
card.pick_when: You want a masked edit that still understands an instruction and reference images — e.g. drop an object from a reference into a painted region, or replace what's under the mask while keeping identity. Use the plain Qwen-Image inpaint when you have no reference and just want the region regenerated from a description.

prompt.guidance: Paint the region to change, then write an imperative instruction. Attached references are image 2 and image 3 — refer to them by number.
prompt.example: (mask over the empty corner) Add the armchair from image 2, matching the room's lighting.
prompt.instructions: Plain natural-language edit instructions (English or Chinese). Only the painted region is regenerated; the instruction and any references describe what goes there. Refer to references by number (your photo is image 1). Recommended: 20 steps, cfg 4.0, euler/simple.
prompt.negative_guidance: Official Qwen-Image-Edit usage passes an effectively-empty negative; the graph derives the negative from the instruction contrast, so no user negative is consumed.

negative.note: Like Qwen-Image-Edit, the negative is the empty-instruction encode over the same image conditioning (real CFG contrast), not a user field.

speed.note: fp8 20B Qwen edit; masked so only the region is sampled but the whole model still loads.

ui_help.note: Paint over the area to change, describe the edit, optionally attach a reference image, and send.
ui_help.good_for: instruction + reference edits confined to a painted region

edit_use_cases: masked instruction editing with references: drop an object from a reference into a painted region, replace or restyle what's under the mask, keep everything outside it

reference.hint: Your photo is image 1; your attached references are image 2 and image 3. Refer to them by number. Example: 'put the chair from image 2 into the masked area.'
